core_obligations: Set up the common framework: write the completed tensor product as the limit over the tensor products of the quotients by fundamental systems of open ideals, identify the kernels of the structure maps as the closures of the ideals generated by the two systems, note that they form a fundamental system of open ideals, and record the dense ring map from the ordinary tensor product (proof lines 1209-1221).
Part (1): show that the kernels consist of topologically nilpotent elements when the two systems do, so that the completed tensor product is weakly admissible (proof lines 1223-1229).

Part (2): choose ideals of definition among the two systems and show that a suitable power of the corresponding kernel is contained in any other kernel, so that it is an ideal of definition (proof lines 1231-1245).
Part (3): observe that a product of two countable index sets is countable (proof lines 1247-1249).

Part (4): identify the completed tensor product with the completion of the ordinary tensor product with respect to the finitely generated ideal generated by the two ideals of definition, and conclude by the algebra statement on such completions (proof lines 1251-1260).

Part (5): use part (4) to get an adic ring with a finitely generated ideal of definition, compute the quotient by that ideal as a finite type algebra over a Noetherian ring, and apply the algebra statement on completions of Noetherian rings; the author marks as omitted the verification that the ideals of topologically nilpotent elements are ideals of definition here (proof lines 1262-1282).
proof_roadmap: Shared setup: limit description, kernels, dense map (proof lines 1209-1221).
Adic with finitely generated ideal of definition (proof lines 1251-1260).
Adic Noetherian in the finite type case (proof lines 1262-1282).
difficulty_reason: For continuous homomorphisms of linearly topologized rings from B to A and from B to C the lemma lists five properties of the completed tensor product: it is weakly admissible when the two rings are weakly pre-admissible, admissible when they are pre-admissible, countably generated as a topological ring when they are, adic with a finitely generated ideal of definition when they are pre-adic with finitely generated ideals of definition, and adic Noetherian in the Noetherian pre-adic case under a finite type hypothesis between the quotients by the ideals of topologically nilpotent elements (statement lines 1186-1207). The proof fixes the common setup once: the completed tensor product is the limit of the tensor products of the quotients by fundamental systems of open ideals, the kernels of the structure maps form a fundamental system of open ideals and are the closures of the ideals generated by the two systems, and there is a ring map from the ordinary tensor product with dense image (proof lines 1209-1221). Each part is then a short verification on that setup: part (1) transfers topological nilpotence to those kernels, part (2) shows that a suitable power of one kernel lies inside any other so that the kernel at ideals of definition is an ideal of definition, part (3) is the countability of a product of countable sets, part (4) identifies the completed tensor product with a completion with respect to a finitely generated ideal and invokes the corresponding algebra statement, and part (5) uses part (4) and computes the quotient by the finitely generated ideal of definition as a finite type algebra over a Noetherian ring, to which the completion-Noetherian statement applies (proof lines 1223-1282). The claim is H2: five statements are proved, but they are parallel consequences of one shared setup and each is a short computation, with the single genuinely external input being the two algebra lemmas invoked in parts (4) and (5).
